title: Unit 3: The Interesting Lore of April Fools' Day

parts.title: Word List 1
parts.content:
Word List 1

Detailed Meanings

😎
lore[lɔːr]n.
a body of traditions and knowledge. (truyền thuyết)
→ According to local lore, a ghost haunts this castle. (Theo truyền thuyết địa phương, một con ma ám lâu đài này.)
😎
April Fools' Day[ˌeɪprəl ˈfuːlz deɪ]n.
the 1st of April, a day for practical jokes. (ngày cá tháng tư)
→ He played a great trick on me on April Fools' Day. (Anh ấy đã chơi khăm tôi một vố ra trò vào ngày Cá tháng Tư.)
😎
practical[ˈpræktɪkl]adj.
relating to practice or action (a practical joke is a prank). ((trò đùa) ác ý, (trò chơi) khăm; thực tế)
→ Earning a living is a practical matter. (Kiếm sống là một vấn đề thực tế.)
😎
punishment[ˈpʌnɪʃmənt]n.
the infliction of a penalty as retribution for an offense. (sự trừng phạt)
→ He received a harsh punishment for his crime. (Anh ta phải chịu một hình phạt khắc nghiệt vì tội ác của mình.)
😎
origin[ˈɔːrɪdʒɪn]n.
the point or place where something begins. (nguồn gốc)
→ The origin of the custom is uncertain. (Nguồn gốc của phong tục này vẫn chưa chắc chắn.)
😎
custom[ˈkʌstəm]n.
a traditional and widely accepted way of behaving. (tập quán)
→ When visiting a foreign country, we must respect the country's customs. (Khi đến thăm một quốc gia khác, chúng ta phải tôn trọng phong tục của họ.)
😎
come about[kʌm əˈbaʊt]phrasal v.
to happen or take place. (xảy ra)
→ How did this situation come about? (Làm thế nào mà tình huống này lại xảy ra?)
😎
Gregorian calendar[ɡrɪˌɡɔːriən ˈkæləndər]n.
the calendar introduced in 1582 by Pope Gregory XIII. (lịch Gregory)
→ Most of the world uses the Gregorian calendar today. (Phần lớn thế giới ngày nay sử dụng lịch Gregory.)
😎
observe[əbˈzɜːrv]v.
to fulfill or comply with. (cử hành, tuân theo)
→ The student organization is effective in ensuring that students observe school regulations. (Tổ chức sinh viên rất hiệu quả trong việc đảm bảo sinh viên tuân thủ nội quy trường học.)
😎
celebrate[ˈselɪbreɪt]v.
to acknowledge with a social gathering or enjoyable activity. (làm lễ kỷ niệm)
→ We will celebrate her birthday with a big party. (Chúng tôi sẽ kỷ niệm sinh nhật cô ấy bằng một bữa tiệc lớn.)
😎
fall on[fɔːl ɑːn]phrasal v.
to occur on a particular day or date. (rơi vào)
→ This year, Christmas falls on a Tuesday. (Năm nay, Giáng sinh rơi vào thứ Ba.)
😎
trick[trɪk]n.
a cunning or skillful act or scheme intended to deceive. (trò chơi khăm, trò chơi xỏ)
→ He got the money by a trick. (Anh ta lấy được tiền bằng một trò lừa đảo.)
😎
play tricks on[pleɪ trɪks ɑːn]phrase
to deceive or play a joke on someone. (chơi xỏ, chơi khăm (ai))
→ The children love to play tricks on their teacher. (Lũ trẻ thích chơi khăm giáo viên của chúng.)
😎
errand[ˈerənd]n.
a short journey to complete a chore. (việc vặt)
→ She sent him on a fool's errand. (Cô ấy đã sai anh ta đi làm một việc vặt vô ích.)
😎
fool[fuːl]v.
to trick or deceive someone. (lừa phỉnh, lừa gạt)
→ You can't fool me with that old story. (Bạn không thể lừa tôi bằng câu chuyện cũ rích đó đâu.)
😎
tape[teɪp]v.
to fasten or attach with tape. (buộc, cột, dán băng keo)
→ They taped a paper fish to his back. (Họ đã dán một con cá bằng giấy vào lưng anh ta.)
😎
prankster[ˈpræŋkstər]n.
a person who plays practical jokes. (người hay đùa nghịch, người chơi khăm)
→ The prankster laughed when his joke succeeded. (Kẻ trêu chọc cười vang khi trò đùa của mình thành công.)
😎
shoelace[ˈʃuːleɪs]n.
a cord or leather strip used to fasten a shoe. (dây giày)
→ Your shoelace is untied! (Dây giày của bạn bị tuột kìa!)
😎
untie[ʌnˈtaɪ]v.
to undo or unfasten. (cởi dây, tháo dây)
→ He knelt down to untie his shoes. (Anh quỳ xuống để tháo dây giày.)
😎
flock[flɑːk]n.
a number of birds of one kind feeding or resting together. (đàn, bầy)
→ A flock of geese flew overhead. (Một đàn ngỗng bay lượn trên đầu.)
😎
cancel[ˈkænsl]v.
to decide that an organized event will not take place. (hủy, bãi bỏ)
→ She cancelled her trip to New York as she felt ill. (Cô ấy đã hủy chuyến đi New York vì cảm thấy ốm.)
😎
innocent[ˈɪnəsnt]adj.
not guilty of a crime or offense. (ngây thơ, vô tội)
→ They hanged an innocent man. (Họ đã treo cổ một người đàn ông vô tội.)
😎
victim[ˈvɪktɪm]n.
a person harmed or injured. (nạn nhân)
→ The victim of the joke laughed along with everyone. (Nạn nhân của trò đùa đã cười cùng với mọi người.)
😎
fall for[fɔːl fɔːr]phrasal v.
to be deceived by something. (mắc lừa)
→ He fell for the trick completely. (Anh ta đã hoàn toàn mắc bẫy trò lừa.)

parts.title: Word List 2
parts.content:
Word List 2

Detailed Meanings

😎
stuff[stʌf]v.
to fill a receptacle or space tightly with something. (nhồi, nhét)
→ He stuffed the shoe with newspapers. (Anh ấy nhét đầy giấy báo vào chiếc giày.)
😎
keep up[kiːp ʌp]phrasal v.
to continue a course of action. (duy trì, tiếp tục)
→ Some practical jokes are kept up the whole day. (Một số trò đùa ác ý được duy trì cả ngày.)
😎
in (good) fun[ɪn ɡʊd fʌn]phrase
not intended to be serious or to cause harm. (rất vui, đùa thôi)
→ The teasing was all in good fun. (Những lời trêu chọc chỉ là đùa vui thôi.)
😎
mean[miːn]v.
to intend to convey or refer to. (có ý định)
→ I'm sorry, I didn't mean to imply that you were dishonest. (Tôi xin lỗi, tôi không có ý ám chỉ rằng bạn không trung thực.)
😎
composite[kəmˈpɑːzɪt]n.
a thing made up of several parts or elements. (hỗn hợp, hợp chất, sự kết hợp)
→ The letters are composites of prankishness and love. (Những bức thư là sự kết hợp giữa tính hay chơi khăm và tình yêu.)
😎
prankishness[ˈpræŋkɪʃnəs]n.
the quality of being mischievous or playing pranks. (tính hay chơi khăm)
→ His prankishness always gets him into trouble. (Tính hay chơi khăm luôn khiến anh ta gặp rắc rối.)
😎
deception[dɪˈsepʃn]n.
the action of deceiving someone. (sự lừa dối)
→ The deception of the salesman turned out to be disastrous. (Sự lừa dối của nhân viên bán hàng hóa ra lại là một thảm họa.)
😎
absurdity[əbˈsɜːrdəti]n.
the quality or state of being ridiculous or wildly unreasonable. (sự phi lý, sự ngu xuẩn)
→ Sometimes a thing is absurd but intriguing. (Đôi khi một điều gì đó thật phi lý nhưng lại hấp dẫn.)
😎
folk verse[foʊk vɜːrs]n.
traditional poetry of a particular community. (bài thơ dân gian)
→ The letters contained old folk verses. (Những lá thư chứa đựng những bài thơ dân gian xưa.)
😎
deem[diːm]v.
to regard or consider in a specified way. (cho rằng, nghĩ rằng)
→ The event was deemed a great success. (Sự kiện được coi là một thành công lớn.)
😎
flattering[ˈflætərɪŋ]adj.
full of praise and compliments. (xu nịnh)
→ It is deemed a most flattering honor. (Đó được coi là một vinh dự đáng tự hào nhất.)
😎
envious[ˈenviəs]adj.
feeling or showing envy. (ghen tị, đố kỵ)
→ Mary was always envious of her younger sister's beauty. (Mary luôn ghen tị với vẻ đẹp của em gái mình.)
😎
acquaintance[əˈkweɪntəns]n.
a person's knowledge or experience of something or someone. (người quen)
→ They are old acquaintances. (Họ là những người quen cũ.)
😎
confine[kənˈfaɪn]v.
to keep or restrict someone or something within certain limits. (giới hạn)
→ The tour group is confined to the planned activities. (Đoàn du lịch bị giới hạn trong các hoạt động đã lên kế hoạch.)
😎
fake[feɪk]v.
to forge or counterfeit. (làm giả)
→ He faked his father's signature on the document. (Anh ta đã làm giả chữ ký của cha mình trên tài liệu.)
😎
issue[ˈɪʃuː]v.
to supply or distribute. (lưu hành, in ra, cấp phát)
→ The school issued uniforms to the players. (Trường học đã cấp đồng phục cho các cầu thủ.)
😎
nonexistent[ˌnɑːnɪɡˈzɪstənt]adj.
not existing, or not real or present. (không tồn tại)
→ He issued tickets for nonexistent parties. (Anh ta phát hành vé cho những bữa tiệc không tồn tại.)
😎
elaborate[ɪˈlæbərət]adj.
involving many carefully arranged parts or details. (kỹ lưỡng, công phu)
→ She made elaborate preparations for the party. (Cô ấy đã chuẩn bị kỹ lưỡng cho bữa tiệc.)
😎
persuade[pərˈsweɪd]v.
to cause someone to do something through reasoning or argument. (thuyết phục)
→ They persuaded her to tell a lie. (Họ đã thuyết phục cô ấy nói dối.)
😎
keep on[kiːp ɑːn]phrasal v.
to continue to do something. (tiếp tục)
→ He kept on laughing at the joke. (Anh ấy tiếp tục cười nhạo trò đùa.)
😎
go around[ɡoʊ əˈraʊnd]phrasal v.
to circulate or spend time with. (đi chơi, lui tới với (ai))
→ He kept right on going around with her. (Anh ấy vẫn tiếp tục đi chơi với cô ấy.)
😎
make a game of[meɪk ə ɡeɪm əv]phrase
to treat an activity as a game. (chơi trò)
→ They make a game of trying to guess who sent the letters. (Họ chơi trò cố gắng đoán xem ai đã gửi những lá thư đó.)
😎
scare[sker]n.
a sudden attack of fright. (sự sợ hãi, sự hoang mang)
→ They created a bomb scare in the office. (Họ đã tạo ra một sự hoang mang về bom trong văn phòng.)
😎
fool around[fuːl əˈraʊnd]phrasal v.
to behave in a silly or irresponsible way. (đùa cợt, lăng nhăng)
→ He had been fooling around with his secretary. (Anh ta đã lăng nhăng với cô thư ký của mình.)

questions.explanation: Correct. Fake means to forge or counterfeit.

questions.content: The quality of being mischievous or playing pranks
questions.explanation: Prankishness is the quality of being mischievous or playing pranks.

questions.explanation: Nonexistent means not existing, or not real or present.

questions.explanation: Confine means to keep or restrict within certain limits.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
Comprehensive Reading

The Interesting Lore of April Fools' Day

The first of April is a special day, on which practical jokes may be played without punishment. The origin of the custom is uncertain, but it seems to have come about in France as a result of change to the Gregorian calendar in 1582.

In sixteenth-century France, the start of the new year was observed on April first. It was celebrated in much the same way as it is today with parties and dancing into the late hours of the night. Then in 1582, Pope Gregory introduced a new calendar for the Christian world, and the new year fell on January first. There were some people, however, who hadn't heard or didn't believe the change in the date, so they continued to celebrate New Year's Day on April first. Others played tricks on them and called them "April Fools." They sent them on a "fool's errand" or tried to make them believe that something false was true.

In France today, children fool their friends by taping a paper fish to their friends' backs. When the "young fool" discovers this trick, the prankster yells "April Fish!" Today Americans play small tricks on friends and strangers alike on the same day. One common trick is pointing down to a friend's shoe and saying, "Your shoelace is untied!" Teachers in the nineteenth century used to say to pupils, "Look! A flock of geese!" and point up. School children might tell a classmate that school has been canceled. Whatever the trick, if the innocent victim falls for the joke the prankster yells, "April Fool!"

The "fool's errands" we play on people are practical jokes. Filling the sugar bowl with salt, stuffing a biscuit with cotton and offering an empty egg shell at breakfast, are good old tricks. Some practical jokes are kept up the whole day before the victim realizes what day it is. Most April Fool jokes are in good fun and not meant to harm anyone. The most clever April Fool joke is the one where everyone laughs, especially the person upon whom the joke is played.

There are also April Fool letters. They are composites of prankishness, deception, absurdity, folk verses, and love. The letters are never signed, but girls, apparently, make a game of trying to guess who send them. To receive an April Fool letter during April, for it can be sent anytime during the month, is deemed a most flattering honor and the contents are shared among envious acquaintances.

April Fool tricks are not, it seems, confined to children. People play tricks in the office. Faking phone calls, issuing tickets for nonexistent parties, and creating bomb scares are all elaborate pranks. The story of a salesman in Rhode Island is said to be the worst trick on April Fools' Day. He had been fooling around with a secretary. He was married and everyone in the office knew about it. The girl was a bit crazy, a real screwball, and one of the other salesmen persuaded her to tell her boyfriend she was pregnant as an April Fool joke. She went in his office and left the door open so everyone could hear her. Her words did make him a little crazy. He thought it was a big joke. Maybe he was happy it was an April Fool joke. But he just laughed and kept right on going around with her.
